headline.text: Poland's president accuses government of court takeover
headline.context: Crisis over control of the Constitutional Tribunal.
headline.vo: Poland is in a political crisis over its top court. President Karol Nawrocki accuses Prime Minister Donald Tusk's government of a forced takeover of the Constitutional Tribunal.

beats.vo: On Friday evening, the court's longest-serving judge said she had suspended its president, an appointee of the former Law and Justice government, and taken charge. Hundreds of protesters gathered outside.

beats.title: How it unfolded
beats.vo: Nawrocki was flying to Senegal, and turned his plane around. Overnight, footage showed him pushing past judges to enter the court. On Saturday, he called urgent talks with party leaders.

beats.quote: This process is difficult, at times even painful, and requires decisive action.
beats.vo: Tusk says his government is restoring the rule of law, after a dispute over judges dating back to 2015. He wrote that the process is difficult, and requires decisive action.

title: Poland's president accuses Tusk government of taking over top court
caption: Poland's Constitutional Tribunal is in chaos after a judge suspended its president, an appointee of the former Law and Justice government. President Karol Nawrocki flew back from a trip to Senegal and called it a forced takeover, while Prime Minister Donald Tusk says he is restoring the rule of law. Nawrocki has called urgent talks with party leaders.
